ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the attached figure, at the top there is a resistor labeled R connecting the upper-left node C and the upper-right node D. The left branch downward from C is, in order, a 10 V power source and a 2 Ω resistor; the right branch downward from D is, in order, a 10 V power source and a 3 Ω resistor; the bottom ends on the two sides are short-circuited by a wire into the same bottom node. The directions of the two 10 V power sources in the figure are the same. Then reason: When writing KVL along the only closed loop, one 10 V power source is passed through as a voltage rise, and the other equal-value 10 V power source is passed through as a voltage drop, therefore the electromotive forces of the two power sources cancel each other, and the total driving voltage of the loop is 0. Thus the loop current I = 0 / (R + 2 Ω + 3 Ω) = 0. The current flowing through the top resistor R is 0, so the voltage across its two ends U_CD = I R = 0.

raw_record.question_text: In the circuit shown in the figure, what is the voltage \(U_{CD}\)?

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the top resistor R connects C to D, and each side branch has a 10 V source above a resistor, with the two sources oriented the same way and the bottom nodes shorted together. Traverse the only closed loop using KVL. The two 10 V sources cancel because one is traversed as a rise and the other as an equal drop. Thus the total driving emf is 0, so the loop current through all series elements, including R, is I=0. The voltage across R is I R = 0, hence U_CD = 0.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: C and D are the top nodes of two side branches sharing the same bottom node; each side branch contains a 10 V ideal source in series with a resistor, and R bridges the two top nodes. Take the bottom conductor as 0 V. Because the two ideal sources have equal value and the same polarity in their respective branches, each branch would place its top node at the same potential, 10 V relative to the bottom, when no current flows. Since C and D are therefore at equal potential, resistor R has no driving voltage and no current. The voltage U_CD = V_C - V_D is 10 V - 10 V = 0.
